title: Stock Market Today Live, September 4: Sensex gains 550 pts, Nifty near 23,950 on easing US Treasury yields; Tata Steel leads gainers - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
Analyst pointing the chart. | Photo Credit: tadamichi

Sensex Today, Nifty 50 | Stock Market Live Updates - Find here all the live updates related to Sensex, Nifty, BSE, NSE, share prices and Indian stock markets for 4th September 2026

At 1:08 pm, Sensex traded 534.88 pts or 0.70% higher at 76,687.74 after hitting an intraday high of 76,883.14. Nifty 50 was up 63.80 pts or 0.27% to 23,937.25 after climbing to 24,005.75.

The broader market outperformed the benchmarks, with the Nifty Smallcap Index scaling a fresh lifetime high in intraday trade. On the BSE, 2,356 stocks were advancing against 1,316 declining, with 146 stocks hitting 52-week highs and 65 touching 52-week lows. A total of 155 stocks were locked in upper circuit and 140 in lower circuit.

SBI Life Insurance was the top Nifty gainer, rising 2.26 per cent to ₹1,753.80. Reliance Industries advanced 1.99 per cent to ₹1,328.40, while HDFC Life Insurance gained 1.78 per cent to ₹543. Adani Enterprises climbed 1.47 per cent to ₹2,943.60, and Wipro added 1.24 per cent to ₹177.90. Finance emerged as the best-performing sectoral index, with insurance and energy heavyweights leading.

On the losing side, HCL Technologies fell 1.17 per cent to ₹1,303.60, while Eicher Motors dropped 1.15 per cent to ₹7,601.50. Maruti Suzuki declined 1.07 per cent to ₹12,720, Bajaj Finserv slipped 0.97 per cent to ₹1,972.80, and Cipla shed 0.88 per cent to ₹1,382.40. Nifty Media was the worst-performing sectoral index. Sudeep Shah, Head of Technical and Derivatives Research at SBI Securities, noted that “Reliance Industries and HDFC Bank are providing key support and currently remain the top contributors to the Nifty.”

Tata Chemicals on Friday said its Kenyan subsidiary is “fully compliant with the regulatory requirements” and has submitted all documentation sought by the government, pushing back after Kenyan President William Ruto ordered the Indian firm to leave the century-old Magadi soda ash operation it has run for two decades. Afcom Holdings plans to acquire four Boeing 777-8F freighters, enhancing its long-haul cargo capabilities and international connectivity.

Jhaveri Credits and Capital has received a letter of award from New & Renewable Energy Development Corporation of Andhra Pradesh Ltd for the supply, installation and commissioning of grid-connected rooftop solar power plants at various government institutions in Andhra Pradesh under RESCO mode.

Inventurus Knowledge Solutions has informed of the resignation of Manisha Kadagathur, Chief Human Resources Officer (Senior Management Personnel) of the company, with effect from the close of business hours on 4 September 2026.

ELGI Compressors USA Inc., a wholly owned subsidiary of Elgi Equipments Ltd, has divested its entire stake in Gentex Air Solutions LLC to the existing joint venture partner, for the purpose of release of exclusivity in certain counties of Texas, US. Shares were flat at ₹633.10 on the NSE.

MIC Electronics Ltd has approved the allotment of fully paid-up equity shares of ₹2 each on a preferential basis to the Neo selling shareholders. The shares are being issued as non-cash consideration towards the acquisition of a 59 per cent stake in Neo Semi SG Pte. Ltd. from Ebisu Global Opportunities Fund Ltd, Unico Global Opportunities Fund Ltd and Tavas Advisory & Consulting (FZE). Shares traded at ₹36.74 on the NSE, down 2%.

Gold prices steady as investors await US payrolls data, eyeing modest weekly gains amid changing interest rate expectations.

Shares of PhysicsWallah Limited were up 5.07 per cent at ₹126.71 around midday on Friday, with intraday highs touching ₹127.80 against a previous close of ₹120.60. The stock opened at ₹123.37 and has seen heavy trading, with over 28 lakh shares changing hands and a traded value of ₹356.52 crore by 12.10 pm.
